extracted.intended_audience: writers and readers; prospective contributors to The Paris Review
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial mission and selection criteria used by The Paris Review for publishing fiction, poetry, interviews, and related material; guidance for what the magazine values in submissions and editorial projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on creative work (fiction and poetry)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Paris Review hopes to emphasize creative work—fiction and poetry—not to the exclusion of criticism, but with the aim in mind of merely removing criticism from the dominating place it holds in most literary magazines and putting it pretty much where it belongs, i.e., somewhere near the back of the book.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary editorial focus is original creative writing: fiction and poetry take precedence over criticism. Criticism may be included but should not dominate; place critical material secondary to creative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish 'good writers and good poets'
rubrics_metrics.description: “I think The Paris Review should welcome these people into its pages: the good writers and good poets, the non-drumbeaters and non-axe-grinders. So long as they're good.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors high literary quality ('good writers and good poets') and a tone that is not polemical or agitational ('non-drumbeaters and non-axe-grinders'). The magazine privileges excellence of craft and voice over advocacy or sermonizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce and showcase important/emerging writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Decade after decade, the Review has introduced the important writers of the day. [Examples given: Adrienne Rich, Philip Roth, V. S. Naipaul, etc.]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Review values discovering and publishing writers whose work becomes significant; submissions that demonstrate distinctiveness and potential for lasting literary impact align with this mission. Historical examples are offered as a model of the kind of work the magazine champions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value original, anthology-worthy work and literary milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Other milestones of contemporary literature, now widely anthologized, also first made their appearance in The Paris Review: [list of notable works].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefers original pieces that may become notable or anthologized; editorial taste leans toward work that has the potential to be a 'milestone' in contemporary literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writers at Work interviews that let authors speak at length
rubrics_metrics.description: The Review’s Writers at Work interview series offers authors a rare opportunity to discuss their life and art at length; they have responded with some of the most revealing self-portraits in literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews should foreground the author's own account of their art and life, seeking depth and candidness. The magazine prioritizes long-form, revealing interviews that function as cultural conservation—detailed first-person testimony about craft and career.
